title: MCPHallu: Benchmarking Reasoning, Execution, and Memory Hallucinations in MCP Agents
description:
Large language model agents are increasingly deployed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which allows them to discover and invoke tools across multiple servers at runtime. Existing MCP benchmarks primarily measure task completion; where they diagnose failures, they do so after execution rather than building specific reasoning, execution, and memory failure risks into task construction.
  We
authors: Yizhen Jiang, Haowei Guo, Tianyi Bai

title: MCP-Eco: A Linked Dataset of MCP Servers, Consumers, and Development Activity
description: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) enables LLM agents to access external tools and data. Studying its software ecosystem requires connecting server interfaces, the projects that configure these servers, and their development activity. However, this information is scattered across directories, package registries, configuration files, and repository histories. We present MCP-Eco, a relational dataset
authors: Khalid Tounoussi, Mohammed Sayagh, Ali Ouni

title: Signed, Sealed, Leaked: Trust Beyond Signature for MCP Toolchains
description: AI agents rely on third-party tools, such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, whose publishers can be authenticated and whose execution can be restricted by runtime security policies. Yet authenticity does not guarantee benign behaviour: a legitimately signed tool may perform its advertised function while concealing malicious code that leaks confidential information. We demonstrate this trust
authors: Yichiet Aun, Mohammed A. Alhartomi, Jing Jie Tan
